nodes.description:
Complexes I, III, IV and V each contain mtDNA-encoded subunits and are reduced together; complex II, built entirely from nuclear-encoded subunits, is relatively spared. In the Australian siblings' fibroblasts, complexes I, III and IV were reduced while complexes II and V were not, and complex I and IV enzyme activity fell by roughly half. In the Leigh-syndrome patient the deficit was strongly tissue-dependent - I, III and IV in cortex, I and IV in cerebellum and basal ganglia, complex IV alone in liver, and only a mild complex IV reduction in muscle.
Two cautions belong with this node rather than in a footnote. First, conventional spectrophotometric respiratory-chain enzymology can be entirely normal in a genetically confirmed patient, in both muscle and fibroblasts, so a normal assay does not exclude the diagnosis. Second, PNPase's RNA-processing function is the more sensitive readout - a point that matters for variant interpretation, not just for diagnosis.
Conformance note: this node conforms to the module's central bioenergetic node in its bioenergetic-decline arm only. The module's upstream node, age-related mitochondrial damage and mtDNA mutation, does not apply to a primary nuclear-gene RNA-metabolism defect, and the module's reactive-oxygen-species arm is not evidenced in COXPD13 patients, so conformance is declared here and nowhere else in this entry.

nodes.description:
Mammalian mitochondria import a small set of nuclear-encoded noncoding RNAs - 5S rRNA, the RNase MRP and RNase P RNAs, some tRNAs and miRNAs - and PNPase is one of the few identified components of that route. Fibroblasts from the founding patient imported significantly less 5S rRNA and MRP-related RNA, and fibroblasts from the Japanese siblings imported less RNase P RNA. Both defects were corrected by re-expressing wild-type PNPT1.
Confidence is PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED because how much of the disease runs through this branch is genuinely contested. The Leigh-syndrome patient's alleles impaired RNA processing with the trimer intact, and the authors of that study note that the role and location of PNPase within human mitochondria remain controversial.

nodes.description: Mitochondria translate thirteen proteins of their own, all subunits of the respiratory chain, on a dedicated ribosome. nodes.description: PNPase is catalytically active only as a trimer, with the active site inside the toroidal core the six RNase PH domains build between them, so the disease alleles converge on the same functional endpoint by different structural routes. Blue-native gels of fibroblasts from the founding patient found no PNPase complex at all; the same was true of the Australian siblings' fibroblasts. Structural work refined that picture: p.Gln387Arg and p.Glu475Gly do not simply prevent oligomerisation, they force a dimer whose KH and S1 domains can no longer engage RNA. Not every allele works this way - the Leigh-syndrome alleles left the trimer intact and instead disabled RNA processing directly, so trimer integrity is not a reliable functional screen.

nodes.description: Bidirectional transcription of the compact circular mitochondrial genome generates overlapping complementary transcripts capable of forming long duplexes. The SUV3-PNPase degradosome normally keeps this species highly unstable. When PNPase is lost the duplexes accumulate and escape into the cytosol - and, notably, that escape is itself PNPase-dependent, so the enzyme has a dual role in preventing both formation and release. This has been shown in patients carrying hypomorphic PNPT1 mutations, not only in knockdown cells. Confidence is PROVISIONAL because it is the accumulation, not its contribution to the patients' clinical features, that has been demonstrated.

meta.association:
PNPT1 encodes the human polynucleotide phosphorylase, a 3'-5' phosphorolytic exoribonuclease whose catalytically active form is a trimer. Each protomer carries two RNase PH domains joined by an alpha-helical domain plus KH and S1 RNA-binding domains, and an N-terminal targeting sequence directs the protein to mitochondria. Disease alleles are missense and act by several distinct structural routes rather than by simple loss of expression.
PNPT1 is unusual among mitochondrial disease genes in carrying three separate inherited phenotypes on different allele classes. Biallelic hypomorphic missense alleles cause this disease (COXPD13, OMIM 614932). A distinct biallelic allele, p.Glu475Gly, was reported in a Moroccan family with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing impairment, DFNB70 (OMIM 614934) - curated separately, though long-term follow-up of one such family found the "isolated" deafness later evolving into multisystem neurodegeneration, so the two may be ends of one spectrum rather than distinct entities. Heterozygous truncating and splice variants in the S1 domain cause dominant spinocerebellar ataxia type 25, a third and clearly separate entity.

evidence.snippet: Other disease-associated hPNPase variants with single amino acid substitutions, Q387R and E475G, disrupt the protomer-protomer interface within the trimer, resulting in the formation of dimers rather than the catalytically active trimers.

nodes.description: Homozygous allele in a patient whose presentation was an Aicardi-Goutieres-like interferonopathy with early-onset encephalopathy, neurodevelopmental regression, secondary microcephaly and white-matter hyperintensities, with a persistently elevated interferon score. Structurally it lies in an RNase PH2 loop near the S1 domain and favours the enzyme's open conformation, impairing RNA degradation without disrupting the trimer.

nodes.description: Homozygous allele in a 34-month-old boy with global developmental delay, hypotonia, hearing impairment, chorea and dystonia, whose imaging added delayed myelination, progressive basal ganglia atrophy and brainstem signal change. Crystallographic modelling placed the substitution at the protein's active site.

nodes.description: Compound heterozygous alleles in two brothers from a non-consanguineous family with severe axonal neuropathy, optic atrophy, intellectual disability and auditory neuropathy. Patient fibroblasts had markedly reduced PNPT1 message and protein and no detectable PNPase complex, and expression of wild-type PNPT1 rescued complex I and IV activity.

nodes.description: The only reported mammalian model of PNPase loss. Constitutive knockout is embryonic lethal, so the work uses knockout mouse embryonic fibroblasts adapted to respiratory deficiency and a hair-cell-restricted conditional deletion. The hair-cell arm reproduces the human auditory phenotype directly; the fibroblast arm reproduces the bioenergetic failure but adds a lesion - complete mtDNA loss - that is not a feature of the human hypomorphic disease.

nodes.description: Sensorineural hearing impairment is one of the disease's defining features and the one with the clearest tissue-level mechanism. It is not universal - it is inconstant in the most severe Leigh-like presentations - and it is also the sole feature of the allelic DFNB70 phenotype, which is curated separately.

nodes.description:
Some patients with biallelic PNPT1 variants have a chronically elevated interferon signature in blood, and at least one presented as Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome with a massively elevated interferon score on longitudinal assessment. Two unrelated patients in a neuroimaging series had cystic leukoencephalopathy resembling RNASET2 deficiency, Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome or congenital CMV - imaging that is characteristic of an interferonopathy rather than of a respiratory-chain disorder.
This node is deliberately typed as a modifier and not as an obligatory step. The interferon response is documented in PNPT1 deficiency and plainly dominates some presentations; what has not been shown is how much it contributes to the encephalopathy of a typical COXPD13 patient. See the corresponding entry under discussions.
